xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5046: Phone app link keeps dropping on 5G: phone re-offers WebRTC sessions repeatedly ('a new offer replaced it' x27) and messages wait to send

plan.title: Phone app link keeps dropping on 5G: phone re-offers WebRTC sessions repeatedly ('a new offer replaced it' x27) and messages wait to send
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: On 5G the phone's link to the home machine churned: the dashboard logged 27 'rtc closing session ... a new offer replaced it' for the phone in a few minutes, the app showed a connection failure, and a composer message stayed 'Waiting to send'. Root cause: PAN-5018's eviction closes every peer connection to the machine on a handshake timeout, and a locally closed RTCPeerConnection fires no 'close' on its data channels, so open streams and in-flight handshakes hang until they time out and evict the next, healthy connection - a self-sustaining loop. The dialer also tears down a merely 'disconnected' connection instead of ICE-restarting it, and the server drops an ICE-restart offer on a known session. Separately, 'Machine links are not running on this dashboard' fires once per dashboard boot because anywhere-boot starts the link supervisor before wiring the link route source. The unknown-peer refusals were the MacBook Air re-linking on 2026-11-03, not the phone.
narratives.Proposal: Phone dialer: destroy every raw channel on a connection it closes (fail fast as 'unreachable'), evict only the connection that carried a failed channel and only while it is current, keep 'disconnected' connections and ICE-restart them on the same session after 2 s (close after 10 s without recovery), accept restart answers, log each step, and expose evict/restartIce/onRecovered. Server RtcTransport: answer a same-session offer as an ICE restart on the existing pc. Shell: on link recovery with the frontend phase not live, call requestReconnect so held messages flush. Boot: wire link sources before supervisor.start(). Prove it with a werift-backed two-restart integration test and a Mac rig iOS Simulator run; update the Anywhere docs.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Server-initiated ICE restart on machine-to-machine links (RtcTransport.dial as initiator)
- A Capacitor network-change plugin or proactive restarts on iOS network events
- Publishing a TestFlight build
- Skip logic for destroyed or unlinked machines in the linked conversation/project/Needs-You syncs
- Any code change for the unknown-peer refusals (MacBook re-link)
- Changes to the frontend composer, flushHeldMessages, or wsTransport backoff constants
- Changes to the overdeck.ai directory worker (services/connect)
- A graceful two-connection handover on the server for a new session id (immediate replacement stays)

autoDecisions.summary: Fix the re-offer loop at the phone dialer and eviction (duplex teardown + per-connection eviction) rather than reverting PAN-5018's eviction.
autoDecisions.rationale: Eviction still recovers a genuinely zombie connection; the loop comes from evicting the wrong connection and from channels that never learn their connection closed.

autoDecisions.summary: ICE-restart a 'disconnected' connection after a 2 s grace, close it after 10 s without recovery.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for ICE restart on network change; 'disconnected' often self-heals within ~1-2 s, and the 10 s cap matches the secure-open timeout so a dead path still falls back to a fresh offer.

autoDecisions.summary: Use createOffer({ iceRestart: true }) on the same session instead of restartIce()+negotiationneeded.
autoDecisions.rationale: Deterministic and testable with fake peer connections; no dependence on event timing.

autoDecisions.summary: Server answers a same-session offer as an ICE restart; keeps immediate replacement for a new session id.
autoDecisions.rationale: werift 0.25.1 restarts ICE on a changed remote ufrag; the phone only sends a new session after closing its old pc, so a graceful handover would only hold dead pcs longer.

autoDecisions.summary: Treat 'Machine links are not running' as a boot-order race and add no destroyed-machine skip logic.
autoDecisions.rationale: The log shows the lines only right after each 'Dashboard listening'; a link that never comes online never triggers onDescriptor.

autoDecisions.summary: No code change for the unknown-peer refusals; document them.
autoDecisions.rationale: Key 4a70be6a806b0ee8 is the MacBook Air's machine key, whose tokens were revoked and re-created during re-links on 2026-11-03.

autoDecisions.summary: Recovery calls requestReconnect (EventRouter forceReconnect) only when the phase is not live.
autoDecisions.rationale: Skips the up-to-10 s backoff for held messages without tearing down a healthy stream or disturbing the first bootstrap.

autoDecisions.summary: Device reproduction on the Mac rig is a checkpoint with a fallback to the integration test output.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requires a reproduction; the rig may be unavailable to an agent, and the automated test reproduces the same two-change sequence.

items.title: Phone dialer destroys every raw channel on a peer connection it closes

expected_outputs: dial-machine.test.ts passes including the two new close tests

narrative.Action: PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-5046.md WI-1. In createMachineDialer add PeerEntry.duplexes: Set<RtcDuplexWeb> (filled in awaitOpen's success branch, removed on the duplex's 'close'), add optional deps.log (default console.warn with '[overdeck] '). closeEntry logs 'rtc <env8> closing session <s8>: <reason>' and, after pc.close(), calls duplex.destroy(new Error(`direct connection closed: ${error.message}`)) for every tracked duplex, then clears the set. Reason: per the WebRTC spec pc.close() fires no 'close' event on its data channels, so RtcDuplexWeb streams and in-flight Noise handshakes hang until the 10 s timeout, which re-triggers PAN-5018 eviction (the re-offer loop). A destroyed-with-error duplex makes FrameReader fail with a non-WireError, which toOpenError maps to 'unreachable'. Ids cut to 8 chars; never log SDP/candidates. Use vi.useFakeTimers for any timeout assertions.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2. Add MachineDialer.evict(raw: RtcDuplexWeb, reason: string): void backed by a WeakMap<RtcDuplexWeb, PeerEntry> set in awaitOpen; it closes the owner only when !owner.closed && byKey.get(owner.key) === owner. In apps/mobile/src/shell/connection.ts secure(), replace `directory.dialer.close(environmentId);` with `directory.dialer.evict(raw, `secure open ${errorCode(error)}`);` keeping routes.delete(environmentId). Eviction codes stay 'timeout' and 'protocol'. Update the connection.ts header (lines 12-14) to say the phone closes the peer connection under that channel. Add evict to the fake MachineDialer in connection.test.ts (line 27) only.

metadata.acJustification: Six criteria: the restart flow has five distinct timer/state transitions plus the candidate-ordering rule the real-UDP tests depend on.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3. Export DISCONNECT_GRACE_MS = 2_000 and ICE_RESTART_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000. In dial() remove 'disconnected' from the dead-state list (keep 'failed', 'closed', entry.closed). connectionstatechange: 'disconnected' -> log 'rtc <env8> disconnected; ice restart in 2000 ms' and start a grace timer (once); 'connected' -> clear timers, and if a restart was in flight log 'rtc <env8> ice restart recovered' and notify internal recovery callbacks; 'failed'/'closed' -> closeEntry (clears timers). restart(entry): only while 'disconnected' and not closed; set entry.remoteSet = false BEFORE sending so server candidates of the new ICE generation queue in pendingRemote until the restart answer (the answer branch sets it true and drains); createOffer({ iceRestart: true }) + setLocalDescription + send the offer on the SAME session; log 'rtc <env8> ice restart sent'; restart timer of ICE_RESTART_TIMEOUT_MS logs 'rtc <env8> ice restart timed out; closing' and closeEntry. onSignal applies an answer only when pc.signalingState === 'have-local-offer'. Add public MachineDialer.restartIce(environmentId): Promise<void> that restarts every live entry for the machine regardless of state, resolves when each reaches 'connected', rejects with the restart-timeout error if one closes; while an entry's offer is unanswered it sends no second offer and waits on the restart in flight. Extend FakePeerConnection with signalingState and createOffer(options). Add restartIce to the connection.test.ts fake dialer. Fake timers only (vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync).

Given a restart offer was sent, when an answer arrives and the state turns 'connected', then the entry stays open and the log receives 'ice restart recovered'
Given a restart offer was sent, when 10000 ms pass without 'connected', then the entry closes, the log receives 'ice restart timed out; closing', and the next dial sends an offer with a new session
Given the pc's signalingState is 'stable', when an answer frame arrives, then setRemoteDescription is not called

Given restartIce(envId) was called and a server candidate arrives before the restart answer, when the answer arrives and the state turns 'connected', then addIceCandidate runs only after setRemoteDescription(answer) and the restartIce promise resolves
Server answers an ICE-restart offer on a known session instead of dropping it

metadata.acJustification: Five criteria: answer, data continuity, log hygiene, unchanged drop rule, and candidate ordering are separate observable behaviors of one protocol change.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4. In RtcTransport.onSignal's known-session branch, replace the 'rtc offer dropped: ... is already open' line: for an offer on a known, open session from the same peer, log 'rtc session <s8> ice restart from <from8>', set known.localSent = false (werift starts gathering the new ICE generation inside setRemote; those candidates must queue in pendingLocal until the answer is sent, which sendLocalDescription already drains), then setRemote(known, 'offer', sdp), createAnswer, setLocalDescription, sendLocalDescription(known, 'answer'), log 'rtc session <s8> answered'; set progress.step so the existing catch logs 'failed at <step>'. Other-peer and closed-session drops are unchanged. werift 0.25.1 restarts ICE on a changed remote ufrag (node_modules/werift/lib/webrtc/src/transport/ice.js 253-264). IMPLEMENTATION CHECKPOINT: write the real-UDP test first; if werift cannot renegotiate the responder pc (throws, or the original data channel stops carrying bytes), restore a drop with reason 'ice restart unsupported', assert that line instead, and state the fallback in the PR body. Real timers here (real UDP), each test under 15 s. Update the module header to list the new line.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5. Add MachineDialer.onRecovered(listener: (environmentId) => void): () => void, firing when an ICE restart reaches 'connected', or when a new entry reaches 'connected' for a machine whose previous entry for the same key closed for a reason other than 'dialer closed' (resume/teardown are not recoveries; the first pc for a machine is never a recovery). New apps/mobile/src/shell/linkRecovery.ts exports installLinkRecovery({ dialer, currentEnvironmentId, phase, requestReconnect }) returning an uninstaller: on recovery of the current machine with phase() !== 'live', call requestReconnect(). In ShellApp.tsx's directory effect install it with phase = () => deriveConnectionPhase(useConnectionState.getState()) and requestReconnect = () => useConnectionState.getState().requestReconnect(), importing from '../../../../src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/connectionState' like the existing resetTransport import; uninstall in cleanup. Add onRecovered to the connection.test.ts fake dialer.

Dashboard boot wires link sources before the link supervisor starts

narrative.Action: PRD WI-6. Create the leaf module src/dashboard/server/services/link-supervisor-wiring.ts (no imports) exporting startLinkSupervisorWired<S extends { start(): void }>(supervisor: S, wire: ReadonlyArray<(source: S) => void>): void; it calls each setter with the supervisor, then supervisor.start(). The test imports only the leaf, never anywhere-boot.ts (its import graph carries directory/link-store/relay state). In anywhere-boot.ts import it and replace `supervisor.start();` in startAnywhere with startLinkSupervisorWired(supervisor, [setLinkStatusSource, setLinkPresenceSource, setLinkRouteSource]) and delete the three later setter calls (~lines 178-180). stopAnywhere unchanged. Root cause: supervisor.start() ran before two awaited follower starts and the route source, so a fast link's onDescriptor -> linked syncs -> linkFetch saw source === null and logged 'Machine links are not running on this dashboard' once per boot (5 lines after each 'Dashboard listening'). No source-text test; spies only.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7. New integration test: phone side = createMachineDialer(hub, { RTCPeerConnection, log }) with RTCPeerConnection from 'werift/polyfill/dom'; machine side = RtcTransport whose onIncoming runs acceptRawChannel (src/dashboard/server/channel-listener.ts) as in tests/integration/anywhere/phone-channel.test.ts; an in-memory hub stamps 'from' like the directory. Case 1: open a link-mode secure channel, round-trip a request, then sequentially `await dialer.restartIce(envId)` twice (each resolves on recovery), after each assert the same secure channel still round-trips bytes; collect logs and assert two server 'ice restart from' lines, zero 'a new offer replaced it', two phone 'ice restart sent'. Case 2: after a fresh dial, evict a raw channel from an older closed connection and assert no new offer is sent. Real timers (real UDP). IMPLEMENTATION CHECKPOINT: if the werift DOM polyfill lacks addEventListener('connectionstatechange'), createOffer({ iceRestart }) or signalingState, drive the same two-restart scenario with werift's native RTCPeerConnection as initiator against RtcTransport (extending rtc-transport.test.ts instead) and state that in the PR body.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-9. docs/ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md: rewrite the 'A failed link is logged on the phone (PAN-5018)' paragraph (~line 201) - a timeout/protocol secure-open failure closes only the peer connection that carried the channel; closing a peer connection ends every channel on it at once; a 'disconnected' connection gets an ICE restart after 2 s before any fresh offer. metadata.sizeJustification: One phone-to-machine link bug whose fix spans the phone dialer package, the mobile shell, the server RTC transport and boot wiring, proved by one integration test and one device run; splitting would ship a phone ICE restart the server drops, or a server change nothing exercises. 18 files; the subsystems are packages/anywhere-channel, apps/mobile, src/lib/anywhere, src/dashboard/server, tests/integration and documentation.
